scenarios.title: Statutory core: couple 25+ · 4 children · UC + Child Benefit
scenarios.description: What you can claim if eligible: one UC couple standard + official child element for each of 4 children + HMRC Child Benefit. No disability, no carer, no housing. Rates are statutory; total is sum of those rates.

lines.label: UC standard allowance (couple, one or both 25+)
lines.eligibility: One joint UC claim — mother and father do not each get a full separate UC award
lines.note: Official monthly rate for couple where one or both are 25+

lines.label: UC child element × 4 (4 × £303.94)
lines.eligibility: Official rate £303.94/child/month × 4 children. Two-child limit abolished 6 Apr 2026 — every child can attract this element.
lines.note: Rate is real (£303.94/mo). “4×” is just count × official rate = £1215.76. Not the same as Child Benefit.

lines.label: Child Benefit (4 children) — HMRC, not UC
lines.eligibility: Separate HMRC benefit. Weekly: £27.05 eldest + £17.9 each other child. Never limited by the two-child UC rule.
lines.note: Child Benefit ≠ UC child element. You can claim both (subject to High Income Child Benefit Charge rules).

lines.label: Housing (UC housing element / rent)
lines.eligibility: Case-specific rent / LHA — not a fixed national rate
lines.note: Omitted from totals so the stack stays comparable

assumptions: 4 children each attract the official UC child element of £303.94/mo
HMRC Child Benefit for 4 (separate from UC)
No LCWRA / carer / PIP / disabled child
scenarios.benefit_cap_note: Rest of GB couple/with-children cap is £1835/mo. This core stack’s UC+Child Benefit can hit the cap if the household is not exempt. PIP is not in this scenario — without a disability/carer exemption the cap can reduce UC.

scenarios.title: Statutory high-support stack (eligibility assumed)
scenarios.description: Ceiling if many eligibility rules are met at once: core UC + disabled-child addition + LCWRA + carer element + max PIP on both adults + Child Benefit. Rare — not a typical family. Housing omitted. Carer’s Allowance not double-counted.

lines.label: UC standard allowance (couple, one or both 25+)
lines.eligibility: One joint UC claim — mother and father do not each get a full separate UC award
lines.note: Official monthly rate for couple where one or both are 25+

lines.label: UC child element × 4 (4 × £303.94)
lines.eligibility: Official rate £303.94/child/month × 4 children. Two-child limit abolished 6 Apr 2026 — every child can attract this element.
lines.note: Rate is real (£303.94/mo). “4×” is just count × official rate = £1215.76. Not the same as Child Benefit.

lines.label: UC disabled child addition (higher)
lines.eligibility: One child meets higher disabled child rules (e.g. higher-rate DLA/PIP daily living)
lines.note: Extra on top of the basic child element for that child

lines.label: UC LCWRA (one adult)
lines.eligibility: Limited capability for work and work-related activity
lines.note: Also an exemption route from the benefit cap when UC is paid for LCWRA

lines.label: UC carer element
lines.eligibility: 35+ hours/week care for someone on a qualifying disability benefit
lines.note: Do not naively add full Carer’s Allowance on top as free extra cash

lines.label: PIP adult 1 (enhanced daily living + enhanced mobility)
lines.eligibility: Non-means-tested personal award — not part of the UC calculation as income in the usual way
lines.note: PIP is outside the benefit-cap “capped benefits” list; a household with PIP is also exempt from the cap

lines.label: PIP adult 2 (enhanced daily living + enhanced mobility)
lines.eligibility: Second adult also on max PIP — rare dual-max case; used as a ceiling
lines.note: Confirms high stack can still be a legal package when disability awards exist

lines.label: Child Benefit (4 children) — HMRC, not UC
lines.eligibility: Separate HMRC benefit. Weekly: £27.05 eldest + £17.9 each other child. Never limited by the two-child UC rule.
lines.note: Child Benefit ≠ UC child element. You can claim both (subject to High Income Child Benefit Charge rules).

lines.label: Housing (UC housing element / rent)
lines.eligibility: Case-specific rent / LHA — not a fixed national rate
lines.note: Omitted from totals so the stack stays comparable

assumptions: Both adults on enhanced PIP daily living + mobility
One adult LCWRA; one adult carer on UC carer element
One child higher disabled child addition
CA not added on top (would usually offset UC)
Because someone gets PIP, the household is exempt from the benefit cap (GOV.UK)
scenarios.benefit_cap_note: Possible stack: PIP is not counted toward the cap, and a household where you/partner/child gets PIP is not affected by the cap at all. So this high stack can legally exceed £1835/mo without the cap cutting UC — provided the PIP (and other) awards are real.
scenarios.cap_exempt_reason: PIP in the household (also LCWRA / carer element are separate exemption routes)

note: Illustrative model. Checksums are arithmetic on published rates, not admin reconciliation of a real claim.
method_notes: Weekly benefits converted to monthly as × 52 / 12.
UC child element £303.94/mo is the official published rate; 4× is arithmetic for a 4-child household.
Child Benefit is a separate HMRC payment (weekly rates) — not the UC child element.
Two-child limit (abolished 6 Apr 2026) only limited UC child elements, not Child Benefit.
Benefit cap: Rest of GB couple/with children £1,835/mo. PIP does not count toward the cap; a household with PIP is exempt from the cap entirely.
High stack with dual max PIP is therefore a possible legal package without cap cut — rare eligibility, not typical.
UC housing element omitted — depends on actual rent.
Carer’s Allowance + UC carer element must not be naively summed as extra cash.
Observed couple-with-children mean is not conditioned on exactly four children.

framing.what_this_is: An illustrative model of which state payments can accrue to a family, using official rates and Birmingham observed UC means.
framing.what_this_is_not: Not a real household. Not linked microdata. Not advice. Not “what every couple with four children gets.”
framing.key_rule: A couple has ONE Universal Credit claim — mother and father do not each receive a full separate UC standard allowance.

observed_vs_core_uc.formula: statutory UC-only (core without CB) − observed couple-with-children mean
observed_vs_core_uc.note: Core UC-only is for exactly 4 children; observed mean averages all couple-with-children households (1+ children, mixed housing/disability). Not like-for-like.

comparisons.naive_ca_warning: Adding full Carer’s Allowance on top of UC carer element overstates cash — CA usually reduces UC.
